title: The multiplicative group, the additive group, and their finite subgroups
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use affine spectra and their contravariant morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum], polynomial rings [def-weil-polynomial-ring], Laurent polynomial rings [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring], and quotient algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Tensor products below are tensor products of commutative $k$-algebras, with the multiplication and universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The *multiplicative group* is the
group scheme
$\mathbf G_m=\Spec k[t,t^{-1}]$, with comultiplication, counit and
antipode the $k$-algebra maps $m^*(t)=t\otimes t$,
$\varepsilon(t)=1$, $i^*(t)=t^{-1}$, in the sense of
[def-sc-group-scheme]. The *additive group* is
$\mathbf G_a=\Spec k[y]$, with $m^*(y)=y\otimes1+1\otimes y$,
$\varepsilon(y)=0$, $i^*(y)=-y$. For $n\geq1$,

$$
\mu_n:=\Spec k[t]/(t^n-1)\subseteq\mathbf G_m
$$

is the *group scheme of $n$-th roots of unity*, and, when
$\operatorname{char}k=p>0$,

$$
\alpha_p:=\Spec k[y]/(y^p)\subseteq\mathbf G_a
$$

is the *Frobenius kernel* of $\mathbf G_a$; both are closed
subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], the closed
immersion being the one induced by the displayed surjections of
coordinate rings.
Here a closed immersion has the affine quotient-ring meaning of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. In characteristic $p>0$, the Frobenius kernel means the kernel in [def-sc-group-scheme] of the $k$-group morphism $F:\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a$ whose coordinate map $k[z]\to k[y]$ fixes $k$ and sends $z$ to $y^p$. This is relative Frobenius after identifying the Frobenius twist of the affine line with the affine line by its coordinate; it does not assert that absolute Frobenius fixes $k$.

proof.text: Put $L=k[t,t^{-1}]$ and $P=k[y]$ using [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Substitution into any commutative $k$-algebra $B$ defines $k[y]\to B$, $\sum a_i y^i\mapsto\sum a_i b^i$, for every $b\in B$, and $L\to B$, $\sum a_i t^i\mapsto\sum a_i u^i$, for every unit $u\in B^\times$. Finite distributivity shows these preserve addition, multiplication and constants; conversely a $k$-algebra map has exactly this formula, being determined by $y$, or by $t$ with $t^{-1}$ forced to its inverse. Use the commutative algebra structure and pure-tensor multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k A)$ with the indicated two coordinate inclusions. Apply the substitutions to $A=L$ with $u=t\otimes t$ (inverse $t^{-1}\otimes t^{-1}$), and to $A=P$ with $b=y\otimes1+1\otimes y$; also substitute $1,t^{-1}$ and $0,-y$ for the counits and antipodes respectively. Thus all six displayed maps are actual $k$-algebra maps. The spectrum correspondence in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] turns them into the required multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms. Lean implementation: affine, map, multiplication and identitySection use algSpec and its braided monoidal structure. The Laurent Hopf algebra supplies the multiplicative group.

proof.text: Check the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] on the coordinate generators. Use the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to identify the two triple tensor products by $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes(b\otimes c)$, with inverse $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\mapsto(a\otimes b)\otimes c$; the unit identifications are $a\otimes c\mapsto ca$ and $c\otimes a\mapsto ca$ for $c\in k$. For $L$, the two iterated comultiplications send $t$ to $t\otimes t\otimes t$; the two counit composites send $t$ to $t$; multiplication after either antipode composite sends $t$ to $t^{-1}t=1=tt^{-1}$, the identity section's value. For $P$, the corresponding values of $y$ are $y\otimes1\otimes1+1\otimes y\otimes1+1\otimes1\otimes y$, $y$, and $-y+y=0=y-y$. These are equal $k$-algebra maps by the generator determination in Step 1; the spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives equality of the scheme morphisms. Thus the displayed data make $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mathbf G_a$ group schemes, with $R$-points $R^\times$ and the additive group of $R$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Lean implementation: construct additiveBialgebra with Bialgebra.ofAlgHom and additiveHopf with HopfAlgebra.ofAlgHom; check the algebra-map equations on Polynomial.X. hopf_group_existsUnique uses hopfSpec, and uniqueness follows from GrpObj.ext and MonObj.ext (multiplication determines the group structure).

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ set $Q=k[t]/(t^n-1)$, a quotient algebra with surjective quotient map by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and write $\bar t$ for its coordinate. For a polynomial $h$, any substitution killing $h$ factors through $k[t]/(h)$: define the value of $[f]$ to be the value of $f$, which is independent of the representative because a difference $hg$ evaluates to zero. Since $\bar t\,\bar t^{n-1}=\bar t^n=1$, substitution gives a surjection $q:L\to Q$ with $q(t)=\bar t$ and $q(t^{-1})=\bar t^{n-1}$. Its kernel is the ideal $(t^n-1)L$: indeed the natural map $k[t]/(t^n-1)\to L/(t^n-1)L$ is inverse to the induced map from $q$, since both composites fix the generator and its forced inverse. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}q$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The formulas $\Delta(\bar t)=\bar t\otimes\bar t$, $\varepsilon(\bar t)=1$, $S(\bar t)=\bar t^{n-1}$ descend to $Q$: their defining relation maps to $\bar t^n\otimes\bar t^n-1=0$, $1^n-1=0$, and $(\bar t^{-1})^n-1=0$. The two iterated comultiplications take $\bar t$ to $\bar t\otimes\bar t\otimes\bar t$; both counit composites take it to $\bar t$; the two inverse composites take it to $\bar t^{n-1}\bar t=\bar t\bar t^{n-1}=1$, its counit value. Equality on the generator proves the group diagrams. The inclusion respects these formulas, so it is a group morphism. On every $R$, its image is exactly $\{u\in R^\times:u^n=1\}$, closed under products and inverses because $(uv)^n=u^nv^n$ and $(u^{-1})^n=(u^n)^{-1}$. Thus it is a closed subgroup scheme in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], with the asserted roots-of-unity interpretation. Lean implementation: rootsCoordinate_pow and rootsRelations verify the defining substitutions; quotient algebra homomorphisms are determined by the residue coordinate. Construct rootsBialgebra and rootsHopf, then apply hopf_group_existsUnique. Laurent map equality reduces by the monoid-algebra extensionality theorem to nonnegative and negative integer powers of the coordinate unit. quotient_surjective proves the Laurent quotient surjective. map_isMonHom proves compatibility by algSpec functoriality and monoidal naturality, and IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective plus faithfulness of Over.forget give the closed subgroup assertion.

source.place: Example Tag 040M (example-roots-of-unity), with the quotient map and subgroup checks expanded; closed immersions: morphisms.tex, Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, so $p$ is prime. For any commutative $k$-algebra $B$, [def-weil-ring-frobenius] gives $(a+b)^p=a^p+b^p$. Put $Q_p=k[y]/(y^p)$ using [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and write $\bar y$ for its coordinate. The maps $\Delta(\bar y)=\bar y\otimes1+1\otimes\bar y$, $\varepsilon(\bar y)=0$, $S(\bar y)=-\bar y$ are well-defined because the relation maps to $\bar y^p\otimes1+1\otimes\bar y^p=0$, $0$, and $(-1)^p\bar y^p=0$. The two iterated comultiplications take $\bar y$ to $\bar y\otimes1\otimes1+1\otimes\bar y\otimes1+1\otimes1\otimes\bar y$; both counit composites take it to $\bar y$, and the inverse composites take it to $-\bar y+\bar y=\bar y-\bar y=0$, its counit value. These generator identities prove the group diagrams. The quotient $P\to Q_p$ is surjective, hence defines a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On $R$-points it is $\{a\in R:a^p=0\}\subseteq(R,+)$; it contains $0$ and is closed under addition and negatives by the displayed Frobenius and sign identities. This verifies [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] without assuming that $R$ is reduced or that $k$ is perfect. Lean implementation: alphaCoordinate_pow and alphaRelations check descent. The binomial correction terms vanish since p maps to zero in every k-algebra (including the zero ring); no nontriviality assumption on these algebras is used. Construct alphaBialgebra and alphaHopf and apply hopf_group_existsUnique. The polynomial quotient is surjective; map_isMonHom gives the group homomorphism and Spec of the quotient gives the closed immersion.

source.place: the alpha_p clause, its omitted verification supplied; binomial identity: varieties.tex, Section Tag 0CC6 (section-frobenius)

proof.text: The substitution $k[z]\to k[y]$, $z\mapsto y^p$, fixes coefficients and defines a $k$-scheme map $F$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; it respects addition because $(y_1+y_2)^p=y_1^p+y_2^p$ [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. Its kernel, by [def-sc-group-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], is $\operatorname{Spec}(k[y]\otimes_{k[z]}k)$ with $z\mapsto y^p$ and $z\mapsto0$. The map $k[y]\otimes_{k[z]}k\to Q_p$, $f\otimes c\mapsto c\bar f$, exists by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Its inverse is induced by $y\mapsto y\otimes1$: this kills $y^p$ since $y^p\otimes1=1\otimes0=0$; both composites fix $k$ and the coordinate, so they are identities. Hence this kernel is exactly $\alpha_p$, including its scheme structure. To check the relative-Frobenius terminology directly, its twist algebra is $k[y]\otimes_{k,F_k}k$ by the same affine-product formula, and the maps $a y^i\otimes b\mapsto a^pb z^i$ and $z\mapsto y\otimes1$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, are mutually inverse $k$-algebra maps (the balancing relation is $ac\otimes b=a\otimes c^pb$). The composite on $k[z]$ fixes $z$ and $k$, while the other composite takes $a y^i\otimes b$ to $y^i\otimes a^p b=a y^i\otimes b$ by that balancing relation. The twist coordinate $y\otimes1$ has additive comultiplication $(y\otimes1)\otimes1+1\otimes(y\otimes1)$ and counit zero, so this identification also respects the additive group law. The relative Frobenius coordinate map $f\otimes b\mapsto f^p b$ becomes $z\mapsto y^p$ under this identification. This proves the asserted kernel interpretation over every field of characteristic $p$. Lean implementation: frobenius_isMonHom checks counit and comultiplication on X using add_pow_prime_eq' and the vanishing of p. For the kernel, alpha_pushout proves directly the pushout universal property of the quotient diagram in CommAlgCat: any compatible cocone kills X^p, so its polynomial map descends uniquely through the quotient. Applying algSpec to the opposite square yields a pullback. The monoidal unit isomorphism identifies Spec k with the tensor unit, and the chosen additive counit identifies its bottom map with the unit section. IsPullback.isoPullback identifies this pullback with GrpObj.ker and its isoPullback_hom_fst equation supplies compatibility with the inclusion. This uses the quotient pushout universal property directly, avoiding an explicit intermediate tensor-product isomorphism.

proof.text:
The group-scheme axioms of [def-sc-group-scheme] hold for $\mathbf G_m$
because the identities $(t_1t_2)t_3=t_1(t_2t_3)$, $1\cdot t=t=t\cdot1$ and
$t^{-1}t=1$ hold in the Laurent polynomial ring; for $\mathbf G_a$ they are the
corresponding identities for addition.
